title: Decline an Outlook meeting with AI and a clear boundary
h1: decline a specific outlook invitation after your review
description: Free a calendar slot by declining an Outlook invitation. Choose the exact date, your explanation and whether the organiser gets a response.
keywords: ai outlook decline with proposed time
answer: **free the calendar slot without making up an excuse.** the bot finds the outlook invitation and declines with your words, optionally proposing another time. outlook emails the organiser by default. dusk classes this as a write, so sending approval does not hold it. tell the bot to ask before declining.
og_line: choose the invitation and the response first.
what:
**say no to the meeting you actually mean.** name the date and organiser, especially when the title repeats. the bot finds the occurrence and can include your explanation or a proposed start and end time.

choose whether outlook should email the organiser; it sends a response by default. a proposed slot still needs a separate availability lookup and the other person's agreement.
uses: decline a supplier demo you have decided to skip
turn down an optional workshop with your chosen explanation
decline a clashing meeting and propose a specific alternative
decline quietly when you choose not to email the organiser

routine.message:
at 16:55 every tuesday, read next week's outlook invitations for supplier demonstrations that overlap another calendar event. show each title, organiser, date and clash here.

propose the explanation "thank you for the invitation; i will not be attending this session." ask me before changing any response. decline only the occurrence i approve and send only that explanation. report the result here. never invent reasons or propose another time without my start and end dates.
routine.needs: outlook with read and write for event lookup and declines, including calendar write permission
routine.output:
decline proposal
- zoe's supplier demonstration, friday 11:00
- organiser: caraway optics
- explanation: thank you for the invitation; i will not be attending this session.
email the organiser only after you agree. invitation unchanged.

steps: connect outlook. allow read and write for calendar lookup and declines.
name the exact meeting, date and occurrence if it repeats.
choose the explanation and whether to email the organiser. ask for review before declining.
open the invitation after the first decline and read its response status. **Pause** if it picked the wrong one.
watch: **put the pause before the decline.** this action can email the organiser, but dusk classes it as a write. sending controls do not hold it.
**use the date and organiser to pick an occurrence.** repeating titles can hide different meetings.
**give both ends of the new slot.** look up availability separately; a proposed time reserves nothing.
**outlook accepted the request. the organiser still has to read it.** success says nothing about their agreement.

faq.q: can it decline without sending an email response?
faq.a: **yes.** ask it to decline without sending a response. otherwise outlook tells the organiser.

faq.q: does the bot ask before declining an invitation?
faq.a: **tell it to ask before declining.** dusk classes the action as a write, so the review step belongs in the routine.

faq.q: can it suggest another time while declining?
faq.a: **yes, with a start and end time.** look up availability separately. the proposal does not book that slot for everyone.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

steps: connect outlook with calendar lookup and decline allowed
ask for one invitation's title, organiser and exact date
choose the response wording and whether to notify the organiser
ask the bot to wait for your agreement before declining

mistakes.fix: put "ask me before you decline anything" in the routine.

mistakes.mistake: rejecting a whole series by a familiar title
mistakes.fix: match the date and organiser to the occurrence you want to decline.

tip.text: want a quiet decline? ask for no response. outlook tells the organiser by default.

items: the date and organiser match the invitation
you chose whether to email a response
the reason contains no invented details
any proposed time has a start, end and separate availability lookup
